title: Onion-Tomato Masala Base Cubes
equip: 1 stainless steel pasta pot/stockpot, Philips hand blender, 60ml-cell silicone tray(s) with lid

items.n: canned whole peeled tomatoes (2 x 400 g cans)
baking soda, only if the base tastes sharp

steps.x: Heat the oil in the stockpot on medium. Add the onions and 1 tsp salt. Cook for 25 min, stirring every 2-3 min, until deep golden. Add 30 ml water at a time if they stick.
Add the carrot and tomato paste. Cook for 4 min, stirring, until the paste turns brick red.

Add the canned tomatoes with their juice, turmeric and the remaining salt. Crush the tomatoes with the spoon. Simmer on medium-low for 30 min, stirring every 5 min, until thick and the oil separates at the edges.

Take the pot off the heat. Blend with the hand blender for 2 min until fully smooth. Keep the blade under the surface to avoid splatter. Taste: it should be sweet and rounded, not sharp. If it is sharp, stir in 1/8 tsp baking soda off the heat (it will fizz), then taste again.
Cool for 30 min with the lid off. Spoon into the 60ml cells and level the tops.
Freeze uncovered for 3 h until solid. Pop out the cubes, bag flat, press out the air and label with name and date.

notes: Use 4 cubes (240 ml) per curry for 4-5 portions. Add them after your whole spices and ginger-garlic cubes. Add 60 ml water, melt and simmer for 5 min, then add the protein.
In the Instant Pot, sauté the spices, ginger-garlic and cubes first, add 60 ml water and scrape the bottom well before sealing to avoid a burn notice.
The base has no chilli. Add chilli to the adults' portions, or plate the child's portion first.
The base is lightly salted at 12 g for 14 cubes. Taste the finished dish before adding more.
Freezer life: 3 months. Cubes thawed in the fridge keep for 2 days. Don't refreeze.
source: None (original; inspired by LifeByMikeG's 5 Flavor Cubes doc)
